title: Tracing & feedback
summary: See what the service did, and what users thought of it. Every LangChain and LangGraph run becomes a trace in LangSmith: a tree of runs with inputs, outputs, timing and tokens. The module traces chains, agents and your own code, groups conversations into threads, controls what is traced and how much, keeps private data out, follows one trace across two services, queries traces, speaks OpenTelemetry, and attaches users' ratings and reviewers' scores to the answers they're about. Nimbus traces only with its own key, through a client that anonymizes and samples, and keeps every rating in its own database.
learn: **Traces**: trees of runs from LangChain, LangGraph and @traceable, with run ids, tags and metadata
**Threads**, and **controlling** tracing: off, another project, local only, sampling
**Private data**: hide_inputs/outputs, anonymizers, secret rules, process_inputs
**Feedback** and **annotation queues**: users' ratings and reviewers' scores on runs
flow:
request ─→ run_config(run_id, thread_id, tags, metadata) ─→ chain / agent ─→ runs ─→ tracing client (anonymizer, sampling) ─→ LangSmith
                                    └─→ answer + run_id ─→ user rates it ─→ POST /feedback ─→ Nimbus DB (+ LangSmith)

path.title: Production path: tracing Nimbus safely
path.summary: Nothing is traced unless Nimbus has its own LangSmith key; then every trace goes through a client that anonymizes emails, phones, cards and secrets and keeps a sample. Answers carry their run id, and users' ratings are stored in Nimbus's database and attached to the traces.

steps.title: Guard
steps.explain: guard_uploads runs before any LangSmith client exists: without Nimbus's own key the SDK's endpoint is pinned to this machine, whatever else the environment says.
production: Keep the key in ai-course/.env (NIMBUS_LANGSMITH_API_KEY), never in code or in a shared .env.

steps.title: Client
steps.explain: tracing_client: the PII and secret rules, langsmith_sampling_rate, the project; run_config gives every answer a run id, thread id, tags and metadata.
production: Add a rule for every new kind of personal data before it reaches a prompt.

steps.title: Feedback
steps.explain: POST /feedback stores a rating against a run id for the signed-in user, and forwards it to LangSmith in the background when tracing is on.
production: Review 👎 answers weekly: they are the next evaluation examples (Module 4).

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Ten conversations with personal data, traced with a default client and Nimbus's client, captured locally.

| | emails uploaded (of 10) | card numbers uploaded (of 10) | traces kept (of 40) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default client | 10 | 10 | 40 |
| **Nimbus tracing client** | **0** | **0** | **8** |

Ten support conversations carried an email address, a phone number and a card number each. Traced with a default client, every email and card number was in the upload. With Nimbus's client (the PII anonymizer, sampling a quarter of traces) none was, and 8 of 40 traces were kept, a share to tune to the traffic. Tracing added 0.64 ms per call at p50, because uploads run in a background thread. Everything was measured against a local capture: nothing was sent to LangSmith. The labs also found two things to design around. LangChain runs inside `tracing_context(enabled="local")` are still sent by the default client, so Nimbus pins the default endpoint to this machine unless it has its own key. And a trace continued from another service's headers uses the default client unless you configure one.
production: Run this check in CI: a new rule or prompt mustn't put personal data back into traces.
